apatosaurus:enwiki:5.title: Apatosaurus (Second Dinosaur Rush and skull issue)

apatosaurus:enwiki:6.title: Apatosaurus (Second Dinosaur Rush and skull issue, part 2)

facts.statement: The genus Apatosaurus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877.
facts.quote: authority: Marsh, 1877

facts.statement: Apatosaurus lived approximately 152 to 151 million years ago during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus lived about 152 to 151 million years ago (mya), during the late Kimmeridgian to early Tithonian age

facts.statement: Fossils of Apatosaurus have been found in the Morrison Formation across Colorado, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Wyoming, and Utah.
facts.quote: are now known from fossils in the Morrison Formation of modern-day Colorado, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Wyoming, and Utah in the United States

facts.statement: The average length of Apatosaurus was 21 to 23 meters with an average mass of 16.4 to 22.4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus had an average length of 21 - 23 m, and an average mass of 16.4 - 22.4 t

facts.statement: Apatosaurus belongs to the Diplodocidae family and is distinguished from Diplodocus by its more robust neck and leg bones.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus is a member of the diplodocid family, differing from Diplodocus proper in primarily robustness in the cervical vertebrae and the leg bones

facts.statement: Apatosaurus held its tail above the ground while moving.
facts.quote: The tail was held above the ground during normal locomotion

facts.statement: Apatosaurus was a generalized browser that likely kept its head elevated while feeding.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus was a generalized browser that likely held its head elevated

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had air sacs that made its vertebrae internally hollow to reduce weight.
facts.quote: To lighten its vertebrae, Apatosaurus had air sacs that made the bones internally full of holes

facts.statement: It is debated whether Apatosaurus used its tail as a whip to make loud noises or as a sensory organ.
facts.quote: Like that of other diplodocids, its tail may have been used as a whip to create loud noises, or, as more recently suggested, as a sensory organ

facts.statement: Brontosaurus was long considered a synonym of Apatosaurus, with its type species reclassified as Apatosaurus excelsus in 1903.
facts.quote: Brontosaurus has long been considered a junior synonym of Apatosaurus; its type species was reclassified as A.excelsus in 1903

facts.statement: A 2015 study concluded that Brontosaurus is a distinct genus from Apatosaurus, though this classification is not universally accepted.
facts.quote: A 2015 study concluded that Brontosaurus is a valid genus of sauropod distinct from Apatosaurus, but not all paleontologists agree with this division

facts.statement: Most size estimates for Apatosaurus are based on specimen CM 3018, which measures 21 to 23 meters in length and weighs 16.4 to 22.4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Most size estimates are based on specimen CM 3018, the type specimen of A.louisae, reaching 21 - 23 m in length and 16.4 - 22.4 t in body mass

facts.statement: A 2015 study estimated the mass of specimen CM 3018 between 21.8 and 38.2 tonnes using volumetric models.
facts.quote: A 2015 study that estimated the mass of volumetric models of Dreadnoughtus, Apatosaurus, and Giraffatitan estimates CM 3018 at 21.8 - 38.2 t, similar in mass to Dreadnoughtus

facts.statement: Some specimens of Apatosaurus ajax, such as OMNH 1670, are 11% to 30% longer than average, suggesting masses between 32.7 and 72.6 tonnes.
facts.quote: Some specimens of A.ajax (such as OMNH 1670) represent individuals 11–30% longer, suggesting masses twice that of CM 3018 or 32.7 - 72.6 t

facts.statement: Size estimates for the largest specimen were revised in 2020 to 30 meters in length and 33 metric tonnes in mass.
facts.quote: the size estimates revised in 2020 at 30 m in length and 33 MT in body mass based on volumetric analysis

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had spatulate, chisel-like teeth suited for an herbivorous diet.
facts.quote: The jaws are lined with spatulate (chisel-like) teeth suited to an herbivorous diet

facts.statement: Exposed enamel on Apatosaurus teeth shows a sugary texture with little wear and no scratches.
facts.quote: Those teeth that have the enamel surface exposed do not show any scratches on the surface; instead, they display a sugary texture and little wear

facts.statement: The holotype of Apatosaurus louisae has a vertebral formula of 15 cervical, 10 dorsal, 5 sacral, and 82 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The vertebral formula for the holotype of A.louisae is 15 cervicals, 10 dorsals, 5 sacrals, and 82 caudals

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had ten dorsal ribs on each side of its body.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus has ten dorsal ribs on either side of the body

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had very long ribs compared to other diplodocids, resulting in an unusually deep chest.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus also had very long ribs compared to most other diplodocids, giving it an unusually deep chest

facts.statement: The humerus of Apatosaurus is stout and resembles those of Camarasaurus and Brontosaurus.
facts.quote: The arm bones are stout, so the humerus of Apatosaurus resembles that of Camarasaurus, as well as Brontosaurus

facts.statement: In 1936, Charles Gilmore noted that Apatosaurus forelimb bones (radius and ulna) remained parallel in life and did not cross.
facts.quote: In 1936, Charles Gilmore noted that previous reconstructions of Apatosaurus forelimbs erroneously proposed that the radius and ulna could cross; in life they would have remained parallel

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had a foot digit formula of 3-4-5-3-2, with three claws on the innermost digits.
facts.quote: The foot of Apatosaurus has three claws on the innermost digits; the digit formula is 3-4-5-3-2

facts.statement: The first Apatosaurus fossils were discovered in spring 1877 by miner Arthur Lakes and his friend Henry C. Beckwith in Morrison, Colorado.
facts.quote: The first Apatosaurus fossils were discovered by Arthur Lakes, a local miner, and his friend Henry C. Beckwith in the spring of 1877 in Morrison, a town in the eastern foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Jefferson County, Colorado.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh initially named the fossils Atlantosaurus montanus before establishing the genus Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: Marsh named Atlantosaurus montanus based on some of the fossils sent and hired Lakes to collect the rest of the material at Morrison and send it to Yale, while Cope attempted to hire Lakes as well but was rejected.

facts.statement: A well-preserved partial postcranial skeleton with many vertebrae and a partial braincase was collected in 1877 and named Apatosaurus ajax in November 1877.
facts.quote: One of the best specimens collected by Lakes in 1877 was a well preserved partial postcranial skeleton, including many vertebrae, and a partial braincase (YPM VP 1860), which was sent to Marsh and named Apatosaurus ajax in November 1877.

facts.statement: Marsh named the genus Apatosaurus after its unique chevron bones, which resembled those of the mosasaur Mosasaurus rather than other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Marsh gave it this name based on the chevron bones, which are dissimilar to those of other dinosaurs; instead, the chevron bones of Apatosaurus showed similarities with those of mosasaurs, most likely that of the representative species Mosasaurus.

facts.statement: Marsh originally distinguished Apatosaurus from Atlantosaurus by the number of sacral vertebrae, claiming Apatosaurus had three while Atlantosaurus had four.
facts.quote: Marsh distinguished the new genus Apatosaurus from Atlantosaurus on the basis of the number of sacral vertebrae, with Apatosaurus possessing three and Atlantosaurus four.

facts.statement: Marsh discovered a larger and more complete specimen at Como Bluff, Wyoming, which he named Brontosaurus excelsus.
facts.quote: Marsh announced the discovery of a larger and more complete specimen (YPM VP 1980) from Como Bluff, Wyoming; he gave this specimen the name Brontosaurus excelsus.

facts.statement: All known Apatosaurus specimens come from the Morrison Formation, where Marsh and Cope conducted their excavations.
facts.quote: All specimens currently considered Apatosaurus were from the Morrison Formation, the location of the excavations of Marsh and Cope.

facts.statement: Elmer Riggs described a well-preserved diplodocid skeleton from the Grand River Valley near Fruita, Colorado, in 1903.
facts.quote: In 1903, Elmer Riggs published a study that described a well-preserved skeleton of a diplodocid from the Grand River Valley near Fruita, Colorado, Field Museum of Natural History specimen P25112.

facts.statement: Elmer Riggs determined that the holotype of Apatosaurus ajax was immature, invalidating the features used to distinguish it from Brontosaurus.
facts.quote: Most of the skeleton was found, and after comparison with both Brontosaurus and Apatosaurus ajax, Riggs realized that the holotype of A.ajax was immature, and thus the features distinguishing the genera were not valid.

facts.statement: Elmer Riggs reclassified Brontosaurus excelsus as Apatosaurus excelsus because he found the distinguishing features between the two genera to be invalid.
facts.quote: Because of this, Riggs recombined Brontosaurus excelsus as Apatosaurus excelsus.

facts.statement: The first Apatosaurus skull was found in 1909 during an expedition led by Earl Douglass at the Carnegie Quarry, Dinosaur National Monument.
facts.quote: It was not until 1909 that an Apatosaurus skull was found during the first expedition, led by Earl Douglass, to what would become known as the Carnegie Quarry at Dinosaur National Monument.

facts.statement: The first Apatosaurus skull found, designated CM 11162, was very similar to the skull of Diplodocus.
facts.quote: The skull was designated CM 11162; it was very similar to the skull of Diplodocus.

facts.statement: Earl Douglass and William H. Holland accepted the skull as belonging to Apatosaurus, but Henry Fairfield Osborn rejected this identification.
facts.quote: The skull was accepted as belonging to the Apatosaurus specimen by Douglass and Carnegie Museum director William H. Holland, although other scientists – most notably Osborn – rejected this identification.

facts.statement: After William H. Holland died in 1934, museum staff replaced the missing head on the Carnegie Museum's Apatosaurus mount with a cast of a Camarasaurus skull.
facts.quote: After Holland's death in 1934, museum staff placed a cast of a Camarasaurus skull on the mount.

facts.statement: The Yale Peabody Museum sculpted an Apatosaurus skull based on a Camarasaurus lower jaw and an 1891 illustration by Marsh.
facts.quote: While most other museums were using cast or sculpted Camarasaurus skulls on Apatosaurus mounts, the Yale Peabody Museum decided to sculpt a skull based on the lower jaw of a Camarasaurus, with the cranium based on Marsh's 1891 illustration of the skull.

facts.statement: John Stanton McIntosh and David Berman concluded that Apatosaurus likely had a Diplodocus-like skull, supporting the earlier view of William H. Holland.
facts.quote: They found that though he never published his opinion, Holland was almost certainly correct, that Apatosaurus had a Diplodocus-like skull.

facts.statement: In 1998, researchers suggested that the Felch Quarry skull used by Marsh in 1896 actually belonged to Brachiosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1998, it was suggested that the Felch Quarry skull that Marsh had included in his 1896 skeletal restoration instead belonged to Brachiosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2020 redescription of material from the Felch Quarry supported the idea that the skull belonged to Brachiosaurus.
facts.quote: This was supported in 2020 with a redescription of the brachiosaurid material found at the Felch Quarry.

facts.statement: The first Apatosaurus specimen with an articulated skull and neck was described in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, the first specimen of Apatosaurus where a skull was found articulated with its cervical vertebrae was described.

facts.statement: Specimen CMC VP 7180 differs in skull and neck features from Apatosaurus louisae but shares cervical vertebrae features with Apatosaurus ajax.
facts.quote: This specimen, CMC VP 7180, was found to differ in both skull and neck features from A.louisae, but shared many features of the cervical vertebrae with A.ajax.

facts.statement: Brigham Young University specimen 17096 is a well-preserved Apatosaurus skull and skeleton that includes a preserved braincase.
facts.quote: Another well-preserved skull is Brigham Young University specimen 17096, a well-preserved skull and skeleton, with a preserved braincase.

facts.statement: Most modern paleontologists agree that Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus belong to the same genus, with Apatosaurus having priority as the name.
facts.quote: Almost all modern paleontologists agreed with Riggs that the two dinosaurs should be classified together in a single genus.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Robert T. Bakker argued in the 1990s that Apatosaurus excelsus should be classified as a separate genus distinct from Apatosaurus ajax.
facts.quote: Despite this, at least one paleontologist – Robert T. Bakker – argued in the 1990s that A.ajax and A.excelsus were in fact sufficiently distinct for the latter to merit a separate genus.

facts.statement: In 2015, Tschopp, Mateus, and Benson proposed separating Apatosaurus excelsus into its own genus based on thirteen differing characters and six species-separating features.
facts.quote: In 2015, Emanuel Tschopp, Octávio Mateus, and Roger Benson released a paper on diplodocoid systematics, and proposed that genera could be diagnosed by thirteen differing characters, and species separated based on six.

facts.statement: Many Apatosaurus species were originally named by Marsh based on fragmentary and indistinguishable remains.
facts.quote: Marsh named as many species as he could, which resulted in many being based upon fragmentary and indistinguishable remains.

facts.statement: A 2005 study by Upchurch and colleagues analyzed the species and specimen relationships within Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2005, Paul Upchurch and colleagues published a study that analyzed the species and specimen relationships of Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus ajax was named by Marsh in 1877 after Ajax, a hero from Greek mythology.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus ajax was named by Marsh in 1877 after Ajax, a hero from Greek mythology.

facts.statement: The holotype for Apatosaurus ajax is the incomplete juvenile skeleton YPM 1860 designated by Marsh.
facts.quote: Marsh designated the incomplete, juvenile skeleton YPM 1860 as its holotype.

facts.statement: Specimens of Apatosaurus ajax date from the late Kimmeridgian to the early Tithonian ages.
facts.quote: The specimens date from the late Kimmeridgian to the early Tithonian ages.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus louisae was named by Holland in 1916 based on a partial skeleton found in Utah.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus louisae was named by Holland in 1916, being first known from a partial skeleton that was found in Utah.

facts.statement: The holotype of Apatosaurus louisae is CM 3018, with referred specimens including CM 3378, CM 11162, and LACM 52844.
facts.quote: The holotype is CM 3018, with referred specimens including CM 3378, CM 11162, and LACM 52844.

facts.statement: All Apatosaurus louisae specimens come from the late Kimmeridgian of Dinosaur National Monument.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus louisae specimens all come from the late Kimmeridgian of Dinosaur National Monument.

facts.statement: In 2015, Tschopp et al. found that the type specimen of Apatosaurus laticollis nests closely with CM 3018, making it likely a junior synonym of Apatosaurus louisae.
facts.quote: In 2015, Tschopp et al. found the type specimen of Apatosaurus laticollis to nest closely with CM 3018, meaning the former is likely a junior synonym of A.louisae.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus grandis was named by Marsh in 1877 in the same article that described Apatosaurus ajax.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus grandis was named in 1877 by Marsh in the article that described A.ajax.

facts.statement: Because Morosaurus is a synonym of Camarasaurus, Camarasaurus grandis is the oldest-named species of that genus.
facts.quote: Since Morosaurus has been considered a synonym of Camarasaurus, C.grandis is the oldest-named species of the latter genus.

facts.statement: Elmer Riggs reclassified Brontosaurus as a synonym of Apatosaurus in 1903, transferring Brontosaurus excelsus to Apatosaurus excelsus.
facts.quote: Elmer Riggs reclassified Brontosaurus as a synonym of Apatosaurus in 1903, transferring the species B.excelsus to A.excelsus.

facts.statement: In 2015, Tschopp, Mateus, and Benson reclassified Apatosaurus excelsus back into the genus Brontosaurus, arguing it was distinct enough to warrant separation.
facts.quote: In 2015, Tschopp, Mateus, and Benson argued that the species was distinct enough to be placed in its own genus, so they reclassified it back into Brontosaurus.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus parvus was first described as Elosaurus in 1902, reassigned to Apatosaurus in 1994, and then to Brontosaurus in 2015.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus parvus, first described from a juvenile specimen as Elosaurus in 1902 by Peterson and Gilmore, was reassigned to Apatosaurus in 1994, and then to Brontosaurus in 2015.

facts.statement: Henry Mook named Apatosaurus minimus as its own species in 1917 based on a pair of ilia and their sacrum.
facts.quote: In 1917, Henry Mook named it as its own species, A.minimus, for a pair of ilia and their sacrum.

facts.statement: A 2012 study by Taylor and Wedel found the material of Apatosaurus minimus difficult to place within Diplodocoidea or Macronaria.
facts.quote: In 2012, Mike P. Taylor and Matt J. Wedel published a short abstract describing the material of A. minimus, finding it hard to place among either Diplodocoidea or Macronaria.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus alenquerensis was named in 1957 by Albert-Félix de Lapparent and Georges Zbyweski.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus alenquerensis was named in 1957 by Albert-Félix de Lapparent and Georges Zbyweski.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus alenquerensis was based on post-cranial material from Portugal.
facts.quote: It was based on post cranial material from Portugal.

facts.statement: Material originally assigned to Apatosaurus alenquerensis was reassigned to Camarasaurus in 1990 and given its own genus, Lourinhasaurus, in 1998.
facts.quote: In 1990, this material was reassigned to Camarasaurus, but in 1998 it was given its own genus, Lourinhasaurus.

facts.statement: In 2015, Tschopp et al. supported the separation of Lourinhasaurus by finding it to be sister to Camarasaurus and other camarasaurids.
facts.quote: This was further supported by the findings of Tschopp et al. in 2015, where Lourinhasaurus was found to be sister to Camarasaurus and other camarasaurids.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus yahnahpin was named by James Filla and Patrick Redman in 1994.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus yahnahpin was named by James Filla and Patrick Redman in 1994.

facts.statement: Bakker made Apatosaurus yahnahpin the type species of Eobrontosaurus in 1998, and Tschopp reclassified it as Brontosaurus yahnahpin in 2015.
facts.quote: Bakker made A.yahnahpin the type species of a new genus, Eobrontosaurus in 1998, and Tschopp reclassified it as Brontosaurus yahnahpin in 2015.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus species have a wider and presumably stronger neck compared to Brontosaurus excelsus.
facts.quote: Among the many notable differences are the wider – and presumably stronger – neck of Apatosaurus species compared to B.excelsus.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh originally classified Apatosaurus in the now-defunct group Atlantosauridae.
facts.quote: Othniel Charles Marsh described Apatosaurus as allied to Atlantosaurus within the now-defunct group Atlantosauridae.

facts.statement: In 1878, Othniel Charles Marsh elevated the group containing Apatosaurus to the rank of suborder.
facts.quote: In 1878, Marsh raised his family to the rank of suborder, including Apatosaurus, Atlantosaurus, Morosaurus (=Camarasaurus) and Diplodocus.

facts.statement: Modern research indicates that Apatosaurus was a fully terrestrial animal, contrary to older theories that it lived partly submerged in water.
facts.quote: More recent findings do not support this; sauropods are now thought to have been fully terrestrial animals.

facts.statement: Studies of its skull suggest Apatosaurus was a ground-height, nonselective browser.
facts.quote: A study of diplodocid snouts showed that the square snout, large proportion of pits, and fine, subparallel scratches of the teeth of Apatosaurus suggests it was a ground-height, nonselective browser.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus likely consumed ferns, cycadeoids, seed ferns, horsetails, and algae.
facts.quote: It may have eaten ferns, cycadeoids, seed ferns, horsetails, and algae.

facts.statement: A 2015 study suggests the necks of Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus may have been used for fighting within their own species.
facts.quote: A 2015 study of the necks of Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus found many differences between them and other diplodocids, and that these variations may have shown that the necks of Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus were used for intraspecific combat.

facts.statement: The single claw on Apatosaurus's forelimb was most likely used for grasping objects like tree trunks when the animal reared up.
facts.quote: The most probable use for the claw was grasping objects such as tree trunks when rearing.

facts.statement: Trackways indicate Apatosaurus could travel up to 40 km per day and potentially reach speeds of 20 to 30 km per hour.
facts.quote: Trackways of sauropods like Apatosaurus show that they may have had a range of around 25 - 40 km per day, and that they could potentially have reached a top speed of 20 - 30 km per hour.

facts.statement: Some researchers believe juvenile Apatosaurus could walk on two legs based on trackway evidence, but this is disputed.
facts.quote: A trackway of a juvenile has led some to believe that they were capable of bipedalism, though this is disputed.

facts.statement: Some studies argue that Apatosaurus necks were not flexible enough to browse high trees and were adapted for low or ground feeding.
facts.quote: Some studies state diplodocid necks were less flexible than previously believed, because the structure of the neck vertebrae would not have allowed the neck to bend far upward, and that sauropods like Apatosaurus were adapted to low browsing or ground feeding.

facts.statement: Matthew Cobley et al. (2013) dispute the idea of flexible necks, suggesting Apatosaurus had limited neck movement and had to move its whole body to feed.
facts.quote: Matthew Cobley et al. (2013) dispute this, finding that large muscles and cartilage would have limited movement of the neck. They state the feeding ranges for sauropods like Diplodocus were smaller than previously believed, and the animals may have had to move their whole bodies around to better access areas where they could browse vegetation.

facts.statement: Taylor found that the neck of Apatosaurus was very flexible, contradicting the view that it was limited in movement.
facts.quote: He found that the neck of Apatosaurus was very flexible.

facts.statement: Calculations suggest Apatosaurus's tidal volume would be 904 liters if it had an avian respiratory system, 225 liters if mammalian, or 19 liters if reptilian.
facts.quote: Paladino calculates its tidal volume (the amount of air moved in or out during a single breath) at 904 L with an avian respiratory system, 225 L if mammalian, and 19 L if reptilian.

facts.statement: An avian respiratory system would require a lung volume of about 600 liters, which fits within the estimated thoracic space, whereas a mammalian system would require 2,950 liters.
facts.quote: An avian respiratory system would need a lung volume of about 600 L compared with a mammalian requirement of 2,950 L, which would exceed the space available.

facts.statement: The estimated thoracic volume of Apatosaurus is 1,700 liters, which could accommodate a 500-liter heart and a 900-liter lung capacity.
facts.quote: The overall thoracic volume of Apatosaurus has been estimated at 1,700 L, allowing for a 500 L, four-chambered heart and a 900 L lung capacity.

facts.statement: James Spotila et al. (1991) concluded that Apatosaurus's large size prevented it from maintaining high metabolic rates due to heat retention issues.
facts.quote: James Spotila et al. (1991) concludes that the large body size of sauropods would have made them unable to maintain high metabolic rates because they would not have been able to release enough heat.

facts.statement: Frank Paladino et al. (1997) estimated that Apatosaurus would need about 262 liters of water per day if it had an avian respiratory system and reptilian metabolism.
facts.quote: Assuming Apatosaurus had an avian respiratory system and a reptilian resting-metabolism, Frank Paladino et al. (1997) estimate the animal would have needed to consume only about 262 L of water per day.

facts.statement: A 1999 study concluded that Apatosaurus grew rapidly as a juvenile and reached near-adult size in about 10 years.
facts.quote: A 1999 microscopic study of Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus bones concluded the animals grew rapidly when young and reached near-adult sizes in about 10 years.

facts.statement: Multiple juvenile specimens of Apatosaurus are known from the OMNH collection.
facts.quote: Multiple specimens in the OMNH are from juveniles of an undetermined species of Apatosaurus

facts.statement: Juvenile Apatosaurus likely had proportionally shorter necks and tails and greater disparity between forelimbs and hindlimbs compared to adults.
facts.quote: Juvenile sauropods tend to have proportionally shorter necks and tails, and a more pronounced forelimb-hindlimb disparity than found in adult sauropods

facts.statement: Computer modeling suggests Apatosaurus tails could produce cracking sounds over 200 decibels.
facts.quote: This computer modeling suggested diplodocids were capable of producing a whiplike cracking sound of over 200 decibels

facts.statement: Baron (2020) argues that using the tail as a bullwhip is unlikely due to the risk of catastrophic injury to the tail itself.
facts.quote: Baron (2020) considers the use of the tail as a bullwhip unlikely because of the potentially catastrophic muscle and skeletal damage such speeds could cause on the large and heavy tail

facts.statement: Apatosaurus ajax fossils are exclusively found in the upper Brushy Basin Member, dating to 152–151 million years ago.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus ajax are known exclusively from the upper Brushy Basin Member, about 152–151 mya

facts.statement: Apatosaurus louisae fossils are rare, known from one site in the upper Brushy Basin Member dating to about 151 million years ago.
facts.quote: A.louisae fossils are rare, known only from one site in the upper Brushy Basin Member; they date to the late Kimmeridgian stage, about 151 mya

facts.statement: The genus Apatosaurus was named by Marsh in 1877.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Marsh, 1877

facts.statement: The type species of Apatosaurus is Apatosaurus ajax.
facts.quote: type_species: Apatosaurus ajax

facts.statement: Apatosaurus louisae was described by Holland in 1915.
facts.quote: subdivision: * Apatosaurus louisae Holland, 1915

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh named the first known species, Apatosaurus ajax, in 1877.
facts.quote: Othniel Charles Marsh describió y nombró la primera especie conocida, Apatosaurus ajax en 1877

facts.statement: William H. Holland discovered and named the second species, Apatosaurus louisae, in 1916.
facts.quote: una segunda especie, Apatosaurus louisae, fue descubierta y nombrada por William H. Holland en 1916

facts.statement: Apatosaurus lived approximately 152 to 151 million years ago during the early Tithonian stage.
facts.quote: Vivieron hace unos 152 a 151 millones de años, durante el Titoniano temprano

facts.statement: Apatosaurus fossils are known from the Morrison Formation in present-day Colorado, Oklahoma, and Utah, USA.
facts.quote: se conocen a partir de fósiles en la formación Morrison de la actual Colorado, Oklahoma y Utah, en Estados Unidos

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had a length of 21 to 22.8 meters and a mass of 16.4 to 22.4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus tenía una longitud entre 21 a 22,8 metros, y una masa entre 16,4 a 22,4 toneladas

facts.statement: Some Apatosaurus specimens indicate a maximum length up to 30% greater than average and a mass between 32.7 and 72.6 tonnes.
facts.quote: Unos ejemplares indican una longitud máxima de 11-30 % mayor que la media y una masa entre 32,7 a 72,6 toneladas

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had one claw on each forelimb and three claws on each hindlimb.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus tenía una sola garra en cada extremidad anterior y tres en cada uno de los miembros posteriores

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had air sacs that made its internal bones full of holes to lighten its vertebrae.
facts.quote: Para aligerar sus vértebras, Apatosaurus tenía sacos de aire que hicieron los huesos internos llenos de agujeros

facts.statement: A 2015 study concluded that Brontosaurus is a valid sauropod genus distinct from Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un estudio de 2015 concluyó que Brontosaurus era un género de saurópodo válido distinto de Apatosaurus

facts.statement: Not all paleontologists agree with the division of Brontosaurus as a distinct genus from Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, no todos los paleontólogos están de acuerdo con esta división

facts.statement: Allosaurus accounted for 70–75% of theropod specimens and was at the top of the Morrison food web.
facts.quote: Allosaurus accounted for 70–75% of theropod specimens and was at the top trophic level of the Morrison food web

facts.statement: Apatosaurus was a large quadruped with a long neck and a long whip-like tail.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus era un gran animal cuadrúpedo de cuello largo, con una larga cola en forma de látigo.

facts.statement: Its front legs were slightly shorter than its hind legs.
facts.quote: Sus patas delanteras eran ligeramente más cortas que las traseras.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus could reach nearly 23 meters in length, 4.5 meters high at the hips, and weigh 22 tonnes.
facts.quote: Los apatosaurios o brontosaurios eran unos de los animales más grandes que han existido en la Tierra, alcanzaban cerca de 23 metros de largo, 4,5 de alto hasta las caderas y tenían un peso de 22 toneladas.

facts.statement: Its cervical vertebrae were less elongated and more robustly built than those of Diplodocus, and its leg bones were much thicker despite being longer, implying a more robust animal.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales eran menos alargadas y estaban más fuertemente construidas que la de Diplodocus, y los huesos de la pierna eran mucho más gruesos a pesar de ser más largos, lo que implica un animal más robusto.

facts.statement: Its tail was held off the ground during normal locomotion.
facts.quote: La cola se mantenía despegada del suelo durante la locomoción normal.

facts.statement: Like most sauropods, Apatosaurus had only one large claw on each front foot and three clawed toes on each hind foot.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los saurópodos, Apatosaurus tenía solo una garra grande en cada pata delantera, con los tres primeros dedos de la extremidad posterior con garras.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Apatosaurus may have swallowed stones called gastrolits to help digest tough plant fibers because its jaws alone were insufficient for chewing.
facts.quote: Para ayudar en el proceso del alimento, el Apatosaurus pudo haber tragado piedras, gastrolitos, de la misma manera que lo hacen muchos pájaros, ya que sus quijadas por sí solas no eran suficientes para masticar las resistentes fibras de las plantas.

facts.statement: A 2015 volumetric study estimated the type specimen CM 3018 weighed between 21.8 and 38.2 tonnes, a mass similar to the Argentine titanosaur Dreadnoughtus.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2015 calculó la masa corporal de algunos saurópodos sobre la base de modelos volumétricos, estimando que CM 3018 pesaría entre 21,8 y 38,2 toneladas, similar en masa a un titanosario argentino llamado Dreadnoughtus.

facts.statement: Giant specimens found in Oklahoma, such as OMNH 1670, were approximately 11–30% longer than the type specimen, suggesting a mass possibly double that of CM 3018, between 33 and 73 tonnes.
facts.quote: Algunos especímenes gigantescos de Apatosaurus hallados en Oklahoma representan individuos de aprox. 11–30% más largos, como por ejemplo el espécimen OMNH 1670, consistente en una vértebra dorsal de 135 cm de alto, que es exactamente un 27% más grande que el correspondiente a CM 3018, lo que sugiere una masa el doble de grande, posiblemente de entre 33 y 73 toneladas.

facts.statement: The first Apatosaurus skull was identified in 1975, decades after the genus was named.
facts.quote: El primer cráneo fue identificado en 1975, varias décadas después de que se le diera un nombre.

facts.statement: Its jaws were filled with spatulate, chisel-shaped teeth adapted for a herbivorous diet.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas estaban llenas de dientes espatulados, con forma de cincel, adaptados para una dieta herbívora.

facts.statement: The first Apatosaurus skull was found in 1909 during Earl Douglass's first expedition at what became the Carnegie Mine in Dinosaur National Monument.
facts.quote: No fue hasta 1909 que un cráneo de Apatosaurus fue encontrado durante la primera expedición, dirigida por Earl Douglass, en lo que se convertiría en el Mina Carnegie en Monumento Nacional Dinosaurio.

facts.statement: The skull was found near the type specimen CM 3018, which was named A. louisae in honor of Louise Carnegie, wife of Andrew Carnegie who funded the field research.
facts.quote: El cráneo fue encontrado a poca distancia de un esqueleto, el espécimen CM 3018 identificado como la nueva especie A. louisae por el nombre de Louise Carnegie, esposa de Andrew Carnegie quién financió la investigación de campo para encontrar esqueletos completos de dinosaurios en el oeste de Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Apatosaurus possessed a Camarasaurus-like skull, based on a disarticulated Camarasaurus tooth found at the exact location where an Apatosaurus specimen was previously discovered.
facts.quote: A pesar de que el apoyo a Holland, se observó que Apatosaurus podría haber poseído un cráneo como Camarasaurus, basado en un diente desarticulado de Camarasaurus encontrado en el lugar preciso donde años antes se encontró un espécimen de Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: On October 20, 1979, the first real Apatosaurus skull was mounted on a skeleton in a museum, the Carnegie Museum, following publications by McIntosh and Berman.
facts.quote: El 20 de octubre de 1979, después de las publicaciones de McIntosh y Berman, se montó el primer cráneo verdadero de Apatosaurus en un esqueleto en un museo, el Museo Carnegie.

facts.statement: In 2011, the first Apatosaurus specimen found with the skull articulated to its cervical vertebrae was described.
facts.quote: En 2011, se describió al primer espécimen de Apatosaurus encontrado con el cráneo articulado con sus vértebras cervicales.

facts.statement: Before the 1970s, scientists theorized that Apatosaurus lived in partially submerged swamps because they were thought to be too massive to support their weight on solid ground.
facts.quote: Hasta la década de 1970 se pensó que los apatosaurios eran demasiado masivos para soportar su propio peso sobre terreno firme, por lo que se teorizó que estos saurópodos debían vivir en pantanos parcialmente sumergidos en el agua.

facts.statement: Recent findings suggest that Apatosaurus was a fully terrestrial animal rather than one that lived in water.
facts.quote: Hallazgos más recientes no apoyan esta idea, ahora se piensa que los saurópodos han sido animales plenamente terrestres.

facts.statement: Studies indicate that diplodocids like Apatosaurus held their necks straight and parallel to the ground rather than upright like a swan to feed.
facts.quote: Un estudio ha descubierto que los diplodócidos tenían cuellos mucho menos flexibles que lo que se pensaba, no lo llevaban erguido como un cisne, sino en línea recta paralelo al suelo, de donde se alimentaban.

facts.statement: Research on Apatosaurus skulls suggests they practiced low, non-selective grazing using their square snouts and fine parallel tooth scratches.
facts.quote: Un estudio sobre los hocicos de los diplodócido mostraron que el hocico cuadrado, los grandes pozos, y arañazos subparalelas finas de los dientes de los apatosaurio sugiere que realizaba un pastorea a baja altura no selectivo.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus likely ate ferns, cycads, seed ferns, horsetails, and algae.
facts.quote: puede haber comido helechos, cycas, helechos con semilla, colas de caballo y algas.

facts.statement: In 2005, Stevens and Parish speculated that Apatosaurus fed on submerged plants from riverbanks.
facts.quote: Stevens y Parish en 2005 especularón que estos saurópodos se alimentaron desde orillas de los ríos de las plantas sumergidas en agua.

facts.statement: A 2015 study suggested that differences in Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus necks compared to other diplodocids might indicate their use in intraspecific combat.
facts.quote: Un estudio realizado en 2015, de los cuellos de apatosaurios y brontosaurio encontraron muchas diferencias entre ellos y otros diplodócidos, y que estas variaciones pueden haber demostrado que los cuellos de apatosaurios y brontosaurio fueron utilizados para el combate intraespecífico.

facts.statement: While some suggested Apatosaurus front claws were for defense, their shape and size make this unlikely.
facts.quote: Una sugerencia es que se utilizaron para la defensa, pero su forma y tamaño hace que esto sea improbable.

facts.statement: The most probable use for Apatosaurus front claws was for juveniles to grasp objects like tree trunks, rather than for feeding or defense.
facts.quote: También era posible que eran para la alimentación, pero el uso más probable de la garra era agarrar objetos tales como troncos de los árboles cuando eran juveniles.

facts.statement: Fossil tracks suggest Apatosaurus could travel 25-40 km per day and potentially reach maximum speeds of 20-30 km per hour.
facts.quote: Rastros de saurópodos como apatosaurios muestran que ellos pueden haber tenido un rango de alrededor de 25-40 km por día, y que potencialmente podrían alcanzar una velocidades máximas de 20-30 km por hora.

facts.statement: Footprints show that juvenile Apatosaurus could run on their hind legs, resembling a basilisk lizard.
facts.quote: Estas pisadas demuestran que los apatosaurios jóvenes eran capaces de correr sobre sus patas traseras, asemejándose a un lagarto basilisco.

facts.statement: The findings about juvenile Apatosaurus running on hind legs were published in 2008, though this is debated.
facts.quote: En 2008 se publicaron los hallazgos, aunque esto es discutido.

facts.statement: Fossil tracks suggest that Apatosaurus lived in herds.
facts.quote: Las icnitas encontradas sugieren que vivían en manadas.

facts.statement: In 2006, Matthew Mossbrucker discovered footprints of a juvenile Apatosaurus at Quarry Five in Morrison, Colorado.
facts.quote: En 2006 Matthew Mossbrucker descubrió huellas de un apatosaurio juvenil en la Quarry Five de Morrison, Colorado.

facts.statement: A 1999 microscopic study concluded that Apatosaurus grew rapidly from juveniles to near-adult sizes in about 10 years.
facts.quote: Un estudio microscópico de 1999 de huesos de apatosaurios y brontosaurios concluyó los animales crecían rápidamente, de juveniles a tamaños casi adultos en unos 10 años.

facts.statement: In 2008, Thomas Lehman and Holly Woodward estimated that an Apatosaurus could grow to 25 tons in 15 years, with a maximum growth of 5 tons in a single year.
facts.quote: En 2008, un estudio sobre las tasas de crecimiento de los saurópodos fue publicado por Thomas Lehman y Holly Woodward. Dijeron que mediante el uso de líneas de crecimiento y proporciones de longitud a la masa, un apatosaurio habría crecido hasta 25 toneladas en 15 años, con un crecimiento alcanzando un máximo de 5 t en un solo año.

facts.statement: An alternative method estimated that Apatosaurus grew 520 kg per year and reached full mass near 70 years of age.
facts.quote: Un método alternativo, utilizando la longitud del miembro y la masa corporal, encontró que un apatosaurio creció 520 kg por año, y alcanzó su masa completa cerca de los 70 años de edad.

facts.statement: These growth estimates are considered unreliable because older growth lines would have been erased by bone remodeling.
facts.quote: Estas estimaciones han sido consideradas poco fiable debido a los métodos de cálculo son no suena;buenos, las líneas de crecimiento más viejas habrían sido borradas por la remodelación ósea.

facts.statement: One of the first growth factors identified in Apatosaurus was the number of sacral vertebrae, which increased to five at maturity.
facts.quote: Uno de los primeros factores de crecimiento identificados de Apatosaurus era el número de vértebras sacras, que aumentó a cinco en el momento de la madurez de las criaturas.

facts.statement: The increase in sacral vertebrae at maturity was first observed in 1903 and again in 1936.
facts.quote: Esto fue observado por primera vez en 1903 y nuevamente en 1936.

facts.statement: A 2013 study by Eva Griebeler et al. concluded that Apatosaurus sp. SMA 0014 weighed 20,206 kg, reached sexual maturity at 21 years, and died at 28 years.
facts.quote: Un estudio realizado por Eva Griebeler et al. en 2013 donde examinaron los datos histológicos de huesos largos y concluyó que el Apatosaurus sp. SMA 0014 pesaba 20.206 kg, alcanzó la madurez sexual a los 21 años, y murió 28.

facts.statement: The same age growth model indicated that Apatosaurus sp. BYU 601 weighed between 17,328 and 18,178 kg, reached sexual maturity at 19 years, and died at 31 years.
facts.quote: El mismo modelo de crecimiento de edad indicaron que el Apatosaurus sp. BYU 601 pesaba de 17.328 a 18,178 kg, alcanzando la madurez sexual a los 19 años, y murió a los 31.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus belongs to the subfamily Apatosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Apatosaurinae

facts.statement: Apatosaurus is classified in the family Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: Family: Diplodocidae

facts.statement: Apatosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: There are 67 recorded fossil occurrences of Apatosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 67
